P01.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy about a queen torn between duty and love. The company performed the scenes in the order the author wrote them and with grave sincerity, adding nothing, but it cut the queen's long speeches of doubt, on which the whole tragedy turns, leaving a brisk run of duels and deaths whose motives audiences could no longer see. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
P01.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P02.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. Its students shared classes and a single sports team drawn from both towns, so there was no contest left to fight over, and nothing was sold or told about the old quarrel; by 1940 few residents could even say which town the bridge had favored. A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
P02.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P03.passage: Starting in 2019, the tenants of a large apartment complex spent two years in talks with its owner over rents and repairs. They had already formed their own committee, but its members found the talks bewildering and handed the work over entirely: at every session the association's director sat across from the owner and bargained on their behalf while they waited outside. Looking back, many residents described the neighborhood association as the tenants' ______.
P03.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P04.passage: Every spring a colony of flightless ground beetles nests on a gravel bar in the middle of a western river, feeding on the seeds of low plants that grow there. The water never reached the nests, and the gravel spit joining the bar to the bank stayed above it, but the flood scoured away the seed plants on the bar and along the bank alike, and by July most of the adults had died beside their dry, intact nests. After surveying the bar in July, one ecologist reported that the year's flood had ______ the colony.
P04.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P05.passage: A sociologist spent three years observing the Saturday market of a small farming town. Its stalls sold the same goods every week, but farmers also left word there of jobs, lost animals, and land for rent, and the stallholders collected these notices and passed each one to whoever needed it, without comment or debate; most of the town's news reached homes this way. By the 1950s, the sociologist concluded, the market mattered to the town less for its trade than as its principal ______.
P05.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P06.passage: In 2015 a small software firm began working with independent restaurants in one mid-sized city. Its website let diners review restaurants, a service national companies had offered there for years, and when a diner and a restaurant disagreed about a bill or a review, both sides accepted the firm's ruling. Diners still dealt with restaurants directly, and the site listed every kitchen alphabetically. By 2018, most of the city's restaurant owners spoke of the firm as their trade's ______.
P06.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P07.passage: Each autumn, several thousand snow geese leave their nesting grounds on the northern tundra and fly some three thousand kilometers south to coastal marshes. That year the flocks, no larger than usual, left together nearly three weeks earlier than in any year on record, rising off the tundra as the first storm swept over their nesting grounds, and they flew the full distance to the coastal marshes ahead of the bad weather. In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.
P07.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P08.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece printed all 212 exactly as written, adding no pictures and inserting nothing between them, but she sorted them into sections on love, faith, and the sea, so that readers met them by subject rather than in their original sequence. Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
P08.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P09.passage: For twenty years, a county library tracked every book and borrower with catalog software that its own technicians had written. Instead of buying a commercial catalog from a large vendor in 2018, the library kept the old program running under its old name, with not one line of its code changed, but laid off its technicians and paid a private firm in another state to operate it. A 2019 audit found that, during the previous year, the library had ______ the program.
P09.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P10.passage: Last spring, the council of one river town replaced the property tax that paid for trash pickup with a monthly fee charged to each household. Bills began with the next month's pickup and explained the charge line by line, and larger, costlier homes paid more than small ones. But a household that put out a second bin owed ninety dollars for it, ten times its hauling cost, a sum the mayor said was meant to make residents stop producing so much trash. Several council members objected that the fee, as written, was ______.
P10.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P11.passage: In the 1930s, two small research teams lowered thermometers into holes drilled in the seabed to measure how much heat escapes from the ocean floor. Their values, too low by a factor of ten because heat leaked away along the drill pipes, confirmed most geologists for thirty years in their existing view that the ocean floor was cold and unchanging, and work on the subject largely stopped until the error was found; no survey since has been calibrated against them. Historians of geology now regard those two measurements as ______ in the history of their field.
P11.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P12.passage: In 1893, during a deep economic slump, a mid-sized industrial city began giving aid to families out of work. Its clerk designed the program alone, ignoring the charity methods then popular elsewhere, and it ran unchanged for thirty years; a family had to visit three offices, file six forms, and wait months for approval, though once approved it received generous weekly payments. In her history of the city, one scholar described its relief program of the 1890s as above all ______.
P12.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P13.passage: In 1983 a small company released the operating system that would run its office computers for the next decade. Its code was freely shared, it was the most advanced system of its day, and it was built as one tightly interlocked program; yet it kept running through power surges and failing disks that crashed every rival system. Engineers who studied the system years later described it, above all, as ______.
P13.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P14.passage: In 2019 an orbiting telescope that tracks the brightness of thousands of stars recorded a drop in the light of one star that had shone steadily for years. The star lost about half its light, sliding down smoothly over an hour and then taking most of a day to climb back, and once that single day was over it returned to full brightness and has stayed there ever since. After studying the telescope's record of the event, one astronomer described the dimming as ______.
P14.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P15.passage: At nineteen, a poet mailed a sheaf of her poems to a novelist she admired, and he answered with a long letter of advice and judgment. One line in it dismissed her poems as clever imitations, and for decades she cited that line in interviews as proof that he had never read her fairly; she ignored all of his advice, was steadily published within two years of receiving it, and burned the letter at forty. Long after the novelist's death, the letter remained the poet's ______.
P15.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P16.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright wrote it ten years before the rest of the play, and its talk of locked gates and lost keys returns in every later scene; it carries the quarrel on without a pause, though the quarrel is settled only in the last act, and audiences have always loved it. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
P16.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P17.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. The glacier shrank steadily every summer from 1950 to 1958, losing a great deal of ice in changes plainly visible in the crews' photographs, but it then thickened again, and by 1965 it had regained its old size, which it has held ever since. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
P17.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P18.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The charge matched the figure on the school's flyer to the cent and was small enough that nearly every family paid it, with nothing returned at graduation, but it was billed again every September for as long as a student stayed enrolled. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
P18.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P19.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. Tenants had long protested by blocking roads; the law created a county board to hear every grievance, and within a year nearly all protest took the form of petitions to that board, which heard them at once, though the quarrels stayed as many and as bitter as before until falling grain prices ended them in the 1840s. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
P19.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P20.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. It had no president, no guards, and no lord or court above it; any household could join a decision, rules were rewritten by vote each spring, and each village in turn took charge of enforcing them, so no single person or place held power for long. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
P20.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P21.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. Unusually, its opening pages stated plainly that each city distrusted the other, listed the ships each had seized, and admitted that the terms might fail; its few clauses on harbor fees, worked out over two years of talks, were enforced for decades. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
P21.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P22.passage: Facing a budget gap in 2021, one rural school district reviewed the twelve bus routes that carried its students to class. It kept running all twelve routes itself, along exactly the streets they had always followed, but it began selling advertising space on the sides of its buses and charging a fare to riders from neighboring towns who used the same stops. By the following autumn, the district had ______ its bus routes.
P22.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P23.passage: Farmers in one northern valley once built hundreds of dry stone walls, and today the walls are coated with lichens, slow-growing crusts of fungus and algae. The crusts spread onto the walls from nearby cliffs after the walls were built, and they grow at no steady rate, but one species withers within weeks whenever sulfur in the air rises, long before crops or people show harm, and the stone beneath it stays bare of soil. In her field guide, one botanist describes these crusts as a living ______.
P23.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P24.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. Its members kept their workshops in every quarter of the city and kept making glassware at the old pace, but the guild won its masters seats on the city council, and the city's nobles began giving its glass as gifts to foreign kings. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
P24.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P25.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum beside the painter's other early work. The painter signed it openly and never repeated the experiment: it sets the flat colors and bold outlines of the Japanese prints he collected against the deep perspective he had learned at the academy, imitating no single artist, and it changed nothing about how he painted afterward. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
P25.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P26.passage: For centuries a dry foothill ridge has been covered by pines, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a drought lasting seven years struck the ridge. Almost every pine survived, and the oaks stayed as scattered as before; the pines' growth slowed during the drought but soon returned to its old rate, and in the next dry spell, in the 1970s, their rings narrowed far less than those of pines on wetter slopes that the drought had spared. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
P26.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P27.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf. She had never touched gold before 1960, when a shortage of yellow pigment left three commissions unfinished on the day they were due; she pressed scraps of leaf borrowed from a framer over the bare backgrounds, where the gold fills most of each canvas and frames the sitters, her close friends, with evident affection. One critic who has examined those late canvases closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
P27.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P28.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, when the local poets had already begun writing in that style, but its editor refused to print unrhymed verse and bought up the town's only other press; the poets, who met in a cafe across the river, kept writing unrhymed verse anyway and waited years for their first books. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
P28.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P29.passage: In 1958 a jazz singer published a memoir of her forty years onstage, years that included a divorce, a bankruptcy, and a long feud with the band she had founded. She mentions the divorce and the bankruptcy but dispatches each in a single breezy quip, and she takes credit for songs her former bandmates wrote, all in smooth, joking prose that she later admitted she had dictated in a week. Reviewing the book in a literary weekly, one critic called it ______.
P29.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P30.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigning for a shorter working day began publishing a weekly newspaper. Its first issue appeared only in 1879, after the last factory had accepted the shorter day and the movement's branches had disbanded; for the next ten years it printed its few hundred former members' memoirs, obituaries, and notices of reunions, and it took no side on any new cause. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
P30.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P31.passage: About nine thousand years ago, a tongue of lava poured into a narrow mountain valley and hardened across the floor where a river had wound in wide loops. The flow blocked the valley just below a low saddle in its western wall, and the river, rising behind the lava, spilled over the saddle within a few years; it now runs above ground through the next valley, still winding in wide loops, and joins a different river. Mapping the valley today, geologists conclude that the lava ______ the river.
P31.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P32.passage: In 1974, one small coastal state set a minimum price that dealers had to pay its fishers for lobster. Lobster prices had held steady for years, so the floor rarely mattered, but officials presented it as a promise that the state would stand behind its fishers for as long as the fleet existed; courts upheld it, it remains in force, and no other fishery has ever been given one. Historians of the fishery now regard the price floor as the state's clearest ______.
P32.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
